key_insight: Anisotropic dilation rescales points along their rays with a direction-dependent profile, and this simple geometric transform can move a distribution to any desired radial summary statistic for optimal regularization.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical way to learn data-adaptive regularizers for inverse problems, improving optimization and denoising performance beyond isotropic scaling.
method: Define an anisotropic dilation that preserves direction but changes radius by a positive spherical profile.
Derive the exact profile that maps a source distribution to a target Gibbs-class regularizer via the radial summary statistic.
Learn the base regularizer and profile jointly with finite-sample guarantees using linear features or sparse ReLU networks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on a controlled 2D family and MNIST denoising, where learning the anisotropic profile further improved results.
watch_item: The approach depends on estimating and parameterizing the directional profile well; in high dimensions, this may be data-hungry and sensitive to model misspecification.
paper_title: The Geometry of Anisotropic Dilation for Optimal Regularization
